**Definitions:**
- **Principal Plane:** A plane at which the shear stress is zero. The normal stresses acting on these planes are known as principal stresses.
- **Principal Stress:** The maximum and minimum normal stresses acting on principal planes.

**Numerical Solution:**
- Given: $\sigma_x = 120\text{ N/mm}^2$ (major tensile stress), $\sigma_y = 60\text{ N/mm}^2$ (minor tensile stress), shear stress $\tau_{xy} = 0$, inclination angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ to the axis of minor stress (i.e., angle with $\sigma_y$ plane).
- Normal stress ($\sigma_n$) on an inclined plane at angle $\theta$:
  $$\sigma_n = \frac{\sigma_x + \sigma_y}{2} + \frac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\cos(2\theta)$|
  $$\sigma_n = \frac{120 + 60}{2} + \frac{120 - 60}{2}\cos(60^\circ) = 90 + 30(0.5) = 105\text{ N/mm}^2$$

- Tangential (Shear) stress ($\tau_t$) on the inclined plane:
  $$\tau_t = \frac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\sin(2\theta) = \frac{120 - 60}{2}\sin(60^\circ) = 30 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 25.98\text{ N/mm}^2$$

- Resultant stress ($\sigma_r$):
  $$\sigma_r = \sqrt{\sigma_n^2 + \tau_t^2} = \sqrt{105^2 + 25.98^2} = \sqrt{11025 + 674.96} = 108.13\text{ N/mm}^2$$
proTip: Pay close attention to whether the angle is given with respect to the major or minor principal axis.
